instruction.text: Now, let’s go to the 1800s! Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: The Industrial Revolution brought new ((++technology fruits)) that could be used to communicate much faster and easier than before.
The telegraph was invented in the 1840s, and meant that ((++messages apples)) called telegrams could be quickly sent across entire countries.

instruction.text: Read the changes made by telegrams and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Railway stations could tell one another when trains arrived and left, preventing crashes.
News could travel much more quickly across the country.
Businesses and governments in different countries could easily contact and work with one another.
Ports and ships could send instant updates on weather and arrival times, helping trade to run smoothly.

instruction.text: Draw a line from the UK to the USA.

finish.text: Queen Victoria once sent a telegram from London all the way to the President of the USA in Washington. This message still took 16.5 hours to transmit, but it would have taken weeks or months before the telegraph!
finish.sound: Queen Victoria once sent a telegram from London all the way to the President of the USA in Washington. This message still took 16 and a half hours to transmit, but it would have taken weeks or months before the telegraph!

instruction.text: Select the telephone to find out more.

feedback.finish: The telephone was invented in 1876. For the first time, voices and sounds could be sent across a short distance.

atoms.b: The telephone? I don’t see why it’s needed! We can already send messages across the globe using ((++telegraph painting)).
But telegraphs can only send written messages. The telephone sends ((++sound light)), and it’s instant!
So I could really ((++speak smell)) and listen to someone in a completely different place? That’s incredible!

feedback.finish: By 1900, the telephone had become the fastest and most popular way to communicate with another person, no matter where they were in the world.
